author: CALLA GIALLOMBARDO Staff Reporter
title: Mary Lou Donuts sprinkles love through Greater Lafayette community - NewsBreak
text:
By CALLA GIALLOMBARDO Staff Reporter ,
1 days ago Donuts sit on display Wednesday in the main area of Mary Lou Donuts. The donut shop is hopeful to get its pastries on shelves in Kroger stores, located in Indianapolis. Meghan Rotter | Staff Photographer What began as a small local donut shop has grown into a recognizable staple of Greater Lafayette’s historical and current community.
“This place has a lot of memories for a lot of people,” Purdue alumnus and owner of Mary Lou Donuts Jeff Waldon said. “We want to keep that story going.”
Mary Lou Donuts has been fueling the Lafayette community with a wide variety of affordable sweets since 1961.
Its donuts are made in-house daily in both Lafayette locations, as well as several locations on Purdue’s campus.
A Mary Lou Donuts sign stands tall Wednesday at its new location. The donut shop currently has two stores in Lafayette, both of which offer walk-in or drive-through options. Meghan Rotter | Staff Photographer “Every morning, we take assorted dozens of donuts to the dining halls,” Waldon said. The pastries can be found in Ford and Wiley dining courts each morning, and occasionally in others, like Earhart.
Mary Lou also supplies weekly donuts to the Purdue Math Department, and brings its donut truck to select campus events.
The donuts are baked and sold for Payless, with the company preparing to connect with more local suppliers in the future, such as Kroger and the Lafayette Farmer’s Market.
Brian Freed, the original founder, believed in providing affordable donuts for everyone.
“He felt like it’s important that anyone (could) come in and afford a donut,” Waldon said.
Waldon works hard to ensure that spirit is present in the company today.
“For me, it’s about maintaining quality. We’ve never changed a recipe. We’ve never changed ingredients. We’ve kept the same vendors,” Waldon said.
